topics.title: Land and Peoples of the Nigeria Area
items: a. Geographical zones and the people
b. The people’s relationship with the environment
c. Main physical features and the impact of geography on human activity e.g., hunting, fishing, farming etc
d. Relations and integration among the peoples of different zones
objectives: i. identify the geographical zones and the people within them
ii. establish the relationship between the people and the environment
iii. relate the impact of geography on human activity in the specific zones
iv. Comprehend the relationships among the various peoples of the Nigeria area

topics.title: Early Centres of Civilization
items: a. Nok, Daima, Ife, Benin, Igbo Ukwu and Iwo Eleru
b. Monuments and shelter systems: (Kuyambana, Durbi-ta-Kusheyi, city walls, moats and palaces)
objectives: i. highlight the main features of the early centres of civilization
ii. examine the significance of various centres
iii. establish the historical significance of the various monuments such as caves and rocky formations

topics.title: Origins and formation of States in the Nigeria Area
items: a. Central Sudan –Kanuri and Hausa, states
b. Niger-Benue Valley – Nupe, Jukun, Igala, Idoma, Tiv and Ebira
c. Eastern Forest Belt – Igbo and Ibibio
d. Western Forest Belt – Yoruba and Edo
e. Coastal and Niger–Delta - Efik, Ijo, Itsekiri and Urhobo
i. Factors influencing their origin and migration
ii. Social and political organizations
iii. Inter-State relations, religion war and peace
objectives: i. relate the different groups of people occupying the various zones to their traditions of origin
ii. determine the inter-state relations
iii. account for their social and political organizations
iv. highlight the differences between centralized and non-centralized (acephalous) states

topics.title: Economic Activities and Growth of States
items: a. Agriculture – hunting, farming, fishing, animal husbandry and horticulture
b. Industries – pottery, salt-making, iron-smelting, blacksmithing, leather-working, wood-carving, cloth-making, dyeing and food processing
c. Trade and trade routes: - local, regional, long distance, including the trade in slaves and trans-Sahara trade
d. Expansion of states
objectives: i. identify the various economic activities of the people
ii. differentiate the economic activities and specialties of the people
iii. relate trade and other economic activities to the growth of the states

topics.title: External Influences
items: a. North Africans/Arabs/Tuaregs
i. introduction, spread and impact of Islam
ii. trans-Saharan trade
b. Europeans
i. early European trade with the coastal states
ii. the trans-Atlantic slave trade (origin, organization and impact)
iii. impact of early missionary activities in the coastal areas
objectives: i. assess the impact of the contact with North Africa on the people and states South of the Sahara
ii. highlight the role of the tuaregs in the trans Saharan trade
iii. examine the impact of early European contact with the coastal people
iv. Outline the impact of the early Christians missionary activities in the costal arears
v. trace the origin, organization and impact of the trans-Atlantic slave trade
